messages.subject: [Boostheaders-devel] Building RStan with BH
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dirk,

On Thu, Aug 7, 2014 at 3:23 PM, Dirk Eddelbuettel <edd at debian.org> wrote:

> Feel free to file an issue ticket as a reminder.
>

The tracker on r-forge for boostheaders seems to not have permissions
enabled for outsiders. But just as a reminder for the next time you update
BH on CRAN that rstan is carrying circular_buffer.hpp,
circular_buffer_fwd.hpp, and the four files under circular_buffer/ . As of
now, it seems that BH has enough of odeint for rstan already and we haven't
added anything from multi_array that I was speculating about last time.

Also, you mentioned that you informally wanted BH to track Ubuntu's
boost-defaults, which is now boost 1.55.0 for Utopic Unicorn and it looks
like it may stay that way for Vivid Vervet, although neither is a LTS
release.

Thanks,
Ben

| was speculating about last time.
| 
| Also, you mentioned that you informally wanted BH to track Ubuntu's
| boost-defaults, which is now boost 1.55.0 for Utopic Unicorn and it looks like
| it may stay that way for Vivid Vervet, although neither is a LTS release.

I have not touched r-forge in about a year.  BH lives here:

   https://github.com/eddelbuettel/bh

and the issue tracker there works.  That is the tracker I referred to in the
August 2014 email you are replying to.

And yes, I noticed that 1.55 is current for Debian and Ubuntu and will switch
at some point, time permitting.  It is not a priority yet.

Focussed suggestions for extension are welcome. What is the name of the boost
library that those files are from?  'dpkg -S' seems to suggest
libboost$ver-dev, so part of core?  Should be easy to bcp out.  I think I
usually point at a library name rather than particular .hpp files ...

Dirk
